name: Password Spraying
description:
Adversaries may use a single or small list of commonly used passwords against many different accounts to attempt to acquire valid account credentials. Password spraying uses one password (e.g. 'Password01'), or a small list of commonly used passwords, that may match the complexity policy of the domain. Logins are attempted with that password against many different accounts on a network to avoid account lockouts that would normally occur when brute forcing a single account with many passwords. (Citation: BlackHillsInfosec Password Spraying)

Typically, management services over commonly used ports are used when password spraying. Commonly targeted services include the following:

* SSH (22/TCP)
* Telnet (23/TCP)
* FTP (21/TCP)
* NetBIOS / SMB / Samba (139/TCP & 445/TCP)
* LDAP (389/TCP)
* Kerberos (88/TCP)
* RDP / Terminal Services (3389/TCP)
* HTTP/HTTP Management Services (80/TCP & 443/TCP)
* MSSQL (1433/TCP)
* Oracle (1521/TCP)
* MySQL (3306/TCP)
* VNC (5900/TCP)

In addition to management services, adversaries may "target single sign-on (SSO) and cloud-based applications utilizing federated authentication protocols," as well as externally facing email applications, such as Office 365.(Citation: US-CERT TA18-068A 2018)

In order to avoid detection thresholds, adversaries may deliberately throttle password spraying attempts to avoid triggering security alerting. Additionally, adversaries may leverage LDAP and Kerberos authentication attempts, which are less likely to trigger high-visibility events such as Windows "logon failure" event ID 4625 that is commonly triggered by failed SMB connection attempts.(Citation: Microsoft Storm-0940)

telemetry.name: User Account Authentication
telemetry.description: Authentication attempts and outcomes for a user or workload account.
telemetry.collection_focus: Collect successful and failed sign-ins, authentication method, application and conditional-access context; distinguish account validation from session creation.

providers.name: Microsoft Entra sign-in logs
providers.scope: Interactive, non-interactive and workload sign-in contexts, subject to tenant features and access.

providers.name: Cloud identity service audit
providers.scope: Issuer-side credential and administrative events where the service supports them.

providers.name: Application audit instrumentation
providers.scope: Application-side use of identities and sessions; design fields without raw tokens.

configuration: Enable/export the required identity sign-in and audit categories from the lab tenant to a protected destination. Document license, role and retention requirements.
Correlate issuance or administrative changes with later sign-ins using non-secret credential IDs, application IDs, user IDs and correlation IDs.
Exclude passwords, bearer tokens, cookies and private keys. Record success, failure, authentication context and application result separately.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: A token creation record is not evidence of token use; a sign-in is not a complete record of every resource access. Some provider-side data is unavailable to the customer.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Per identity and application: first-seen clients/resources, changes in authentication failures and session patterns, and unusual permission changes. Separate automation, travel, shared egress and identity-provider policy changes.

strategies.name: Distributed Password Spraying via Authentication Failures Across Multiple Accounts

analytics.name: Analytic 1336
analytics.guidance: A high volume of authentication failures using a single password (or small set) across many different user accounts within a defined time window

tuning.description: Number of distinct accounts a password is used against before alerting
Window over which the correlation is measured (e.g., 10 mins)
Limit detection to sensitive or monitored user groups (e.g., Admins)

analytics.name: Analytic 1337
analytics.guidance: Authentication failures across different accounts using a repeated or similar password via SSH or PAM stack within a short window

tuning.description: Repetition or minor variation of the same password across user attempts
Length of time to observe distributed spray attempts from single source

analytics.name: Analytic 1338
analytics.guidance: Multiple failed login attempts across different users using common password patterns (e.g., 'Welcome2023')

tuning.description: Total number of attempts before alerting
List of passwords considered suspicious due to widespread use

analytics.name: Analytic 1339
analytics.guidance: Sign-in failures across enterprise SSO applications or SaaS platforms from same IP address using the same password against multiple user identities

tuning.description: Use geolocation mismatches to strengthen signal
Proportion of total user base affected to filter noise

analytics.name: Analytic 1340
analytics.guidance: Authentication failure logs on routers/switches showing repeated use of default or common passwords across multiple accounts

tuning.description: Cluster of failed attempts in short period indicating spray
Limit detection to console/SSH vs web UI interfaces

analytics.name: Analytic 1341
analytics.guidance: Repeated failed authentication attempts to container APIs, control planes, or login shells across many user names using same password

tuning.description: Detect spray attempts scoped to single pod vs full cluster
Limit detection to non-service accounts to reduce noise

analytics.name: Analytic 1342
analytics.guidance: Failed authentication attempts across user mailboxes using identical or common passwords (e.g., OWA brute attempts)

tuning.description: Threshold on mailbox login failures by same IP
Match target usernames to common spray dictionaries

analytics.name: Analytic 1343
analytics.guidance: SaaS applications receiving authentication failures for dozens of accounts using same password or login signature

tuning.description: Restrict detection to identity providers or select high-risk SaaS platforms
Adjust based on size and role of account pool

mitigations.description: Refer to NIST guidelines when creating password policies. (Citation: NIST 800-63-3)

references.description: Temoshok, D., et al. (July 2025). SP 800-63-4, Digital Identity Guidelines. Retrieved July 29, 2026.

mitigations.name: Multi-factor Authentication
mitigations.description: Use multi-factor authentication. Where possible, also enable multi-factor authentication on externally facing services.

mitigations.name: Account Use Policies
mitigations.description: Set account lockout policies after a certain number of failed login attempts to prevent passwords from being guessed. Too strict a policy may create a denial of service condition and render environments un-usable, with all accounts used in the brute force being locked-out. Use conditional access policies to block logins from non-compliant devices or from outside defined organization IP ranges.(Citation: Microsoft Common Conditional Access Policies) Consider blocking risky authentication requests, such as those originating from anonymizing services/proxies.(Citation: Okta Block Anonymizing Services)

references.description: Microsoft. (2022, December 14). Conditional Access templates. Retrieved February 21, 2023.

candidates.name: Password Spray (DomainPasswordSpray)
candidates.description:
Perform a domain password spray using the DomainPasswordSpray tool. It will try a single password against all users in the domain

https://github.com/dafthack/DomainPasswordSpray

candidates.name: WinPwn - DomainPasswordSpray Attacks
candidates.description: DomainPasswordSpray Attacks technique via function of WinPwn

candidates.name: Password Spray all Domain Users
candidates.description:
CAUTION! Be very careful to not exceed the password lockout threshold for users in the domain by running this test too frequently.
This atomic attempts to map the IPC$ share on one of the Domain Controllers using a password of Spring2020 for each user in the %temp%\users.txt list. Any successful authentications will be printed to the screen with a message like "[*] username:password", whereas a failed auth will simply print a period. Use the input arguments to specify your own password to use for the password spray.
Use the get_prereq_command's to create a list of all domain users in the temp directory called users.txt.
See the "Windows FOR Loop Password Spraying Made Easy" blog by @OrOneEqualsOne for more details on how these spray commands work. https://medium.com/walmartlabs/windows-for-loop-password-spraying-made-easy-c8cd4ebb86b5

password.description: The password to try for each user in users.txt

dependencies.description: List of domain users to password spray must exits at %temp%\users.txt

candidates.name: AWS - Password Spray an AWS using GoAWSConsoleSpray
candidates.description: GoAWSConsoleSpray is a tool that can be used to spray AWS IAM Console Credentials in order to identify a valid login for a user account built by WhiteOakSecurity. For more details reagrding the tool, check - https://www.whiteoaksecurity.com/blog/goawsconsolespray-password-spraying-tool/

candidates.name: Password spray all Azure AD users with a single password
candidates.description:
Attempt to brute force all Azure AD users with a single password (called "password spraying") via AzureAD Powershell module.
Valid credentials are only needed to fetch the list of Azure AD users.

password.description: Single password we will attempt to auth with (if you need several passwords, then it is a bruteforce so see T1110.001)

valid_username.description: Valid username to retrieve Azure AD users. We encourage users running this atomic to add a valid microsoft account domain; for eg <valid_test_user>@<valid_ms_account.com>

valid_password.description: Valid password to authenticate as valid_username in the <valid_ms_account>

candidates.name: Password Spray Invoke-DomainPasswordSpray Light
candidates.description:
Perform a domain password spray using the same core method of the [DomainPasswordSpray tool](https://github.com/dafthack/DomainPasswordSpray) 
but without all the extra code that makes the script get blocked by many AVs. 
This atomic test will attempt a single password against all users in a password list at $env:Temp\usersdpsLight.txt. You can create this file manually
or with the automated prereq_command. The prereq_command will limit the user list to 200 users by default to help you avoid massive account lockout.

user_limit.description: The max number of users to put in the list when running the prereq_command

password.description: The password to try for each user in users.txt

candidates.name: Password Spray using Kerbrute Tool
candidates.description: Test a single password against a list of users

domaincontroller.description: Domain controller where test will be run

domain.description: Domain where you will be testing

candidates.name: Password spray all Active Directory domain users with a single password via LDAP against domain controller (NTLM or Kerberos)
candidates.description:
Attempt to brute force all Active Directory domain users with a single password (called "password spraying") on a domain controller, via LDAP, with NTLM or Kerberos

Prerequisite: AD RSAT PowerShell module is needed and it must run under a domain user (to fetch the list of all domain users)

password.description: single password we will attempt to auth with (if you need several passwords, then it is a bruteforce so see T1110.001)

auth.description: authentication method to choose between "NTLM" and "Kerberos"

candidates.name: Password Spray Microsoft Online Accounts with MSOLSpray (Azure/O365)
candidates.description: This test attempts to brute force a list of Microsoft Online (Azure/O365) users with a single password via the MSOLSpray Powershell module.

password.description: Single password to try against the list of user accounts

user_list.description: File path to list of users (one per line, formatted as user@subdomain.onmicrosoft.com)

dependencies.description: MSOLSpray module must exist in PathToAtomicsFolder\..\ExternalPayloads.

simulation.prerequisites: Use disposable lab hosts and test accounts, explicit target allowlists, a clean snapshot, bounded egress and a restore plan. Review every candidate and dependency before any execution.

synthetic.purpose: Collection/parser contract exercise, NOT a positive example or detection of this TTP.
